title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Village of Noble Board of Trustees approved a $147,048.05 final payment for a sewer lagoon improvement project at their meeting on Monday.

Trustees discussed the status of the Water Fund remaining with a negative balance.  The board agreed to review additional information at a future Water Committee meeting.

Brandon Bridges of Charleston Engineering presented the final application for payment for the sewer lagoon bypass piping, sludge removal and baffle replacement project.  The board approved the final payment of $147,048.05 to Followell Construction.

Trustees announced that community Halloween activities are scheduled for October 30th at Noble Park, Trick-or-Treat hours for the village will be October 31st from 6 to 8 pm.

The next regular meeting of the Noble Village Board is scheduled for September 28th at Noble Village Hall.

title: FLORA HIGH SCHOOL HOMECOMING
full_story:
Flora High School is gearing up for Homecoming week which will start with Dress up days.

Monday will be Movie Star Monday, where students will dress as their favorite movie star.  Tuesday will be Something you Can’t Wear Anywhere Else day.  Wednesday will be Color War Day, Seniors will wear black, Juniors will wear yellow, Sophomores will wear Red, and Freshmen will wear Green.  Faculty will be dressed in Blue.  Thursday will be Dolly Parton Day and Pink Out Day. and Friday will be Crazy Orange and Blue Day.

The Homecoming Parade will be held Wednesday night, beginning at 7:30 pm through downtown Flora.  The parade will start at the Depot with line up at 7, and end at the corner of North Avenue and Mill Street.  The Flora Fire Department will be selling a pork burgers, chips, and water starting at 5 pm, cost is by donation.  Class Competitions will then be held on Dancey Field at 8 with the bonfire to follow.

Friday night, at 7 pm will be the Homecoming Football game at Dancey Field, against the Eldorado Eagles with the Homecoming court announced during half time of the game.

The student body has chosen the Queen candidates of Myra Sloan, Marli Myers, Qynlin Brown, Danica Conklin and Rosalyn Stanford.  King Candidates are Guy Arnold, Rylan Billingsly, Kehlin Crawford, Brennan O’Donnell, and Kormik Massie.  The Junior Class attendants are Morgan Irmen, Mylea Jones, Kennedy Zimmerman, Tyler Earnst, Braxton Oestrich, and Ashton Williams.  The Sophomores Class attendants are Vayda Kohn and Carson Smith.  The Freshmen Class Attendants are Halle Patridge and Sawyer Murbarger.

The coronation of the King and Queen will be held next Saturday night, in the FHS Gym.  Dance opens at 7 for students, parents are welcome to enter at 7:15, coronation begins at 7:30 and dance is from 8 to 10 pm.

title: FORD TOWN FUN FEST 2026
full_story:
The location for the festival is in front of the Flora Public Library and Food trucks will be set up on East 2nd Street.

The event starts with a Cruise in at 5 pm, starting at the parking lot of Beck’s Auto Sales with dash plaques to the first 100 entries.  The car show is open to any make or model of car.  They will be cruising through town and past Heritage Woods so the residents can look at the vehicles.  Food trucks inflatables and family yard games will be available at Library Park from 5 to 8 pm, and Just for Spite Unplugged will be playing from 6 to 9 pm.

Tomorrow the Clay County Cruisers will have a Car Show with registration from 9 until Noon.  The car show registration is $15 and there will be awards for the top 75 plus 5 specialty awards.  For Car show information call 618-676-4005, 618-662-5646 or 618-676-7732.  Dash plaques will be given to the first 100 entrants.  Craft and food vendors, inflatables, and games will also open at 9 am.  There are also commemorative T-shirts available for $20.

At noon the craft brew and chili cookoff sampling will begin and the dunking booth will open.  Car show awards are at 3 pm and craft beer and chili judging will begin at 4 pm.  The winner of the Chili Cookoff will win a $100 gift card and have their name engraved on the Chili Cookoff Plaque in City Hall.  For more information call Arriel at the Chamber Office at 618-662-5646.

title: BOBCAT HEAD BASKETBALL COACH
full_story:
Chris Forrest was approved as Frontier Community College’s first head men’s basketball coach during Tuesday night’s Illinois Eastern Community Colleges Board of Trustees Meeting.  Forrest joins FCC from Missouri Baptist University in Arnold, Missouri, where he served as associate head men’s basketball coach for the Spartans.

Forrest said the opportunity to establish a new program and help shape its future drew him to Frontier.  Forrest’s path to coaching began after an injury ended his time playing basketball in Belgium, shifting his focus to coaching and player development.  Southern Illinois has a rich basketball tradition, and Frontier Community College Athletic Director Jeremy Ellis sees the addition of the sport as an important milestone for the college.

The search for Frontier’s first men’s basketball head coach attracted a strong pool of applicants from across the nation.  Ellis said Forrest stood out for his commitment to community, emphasis on character and diverse coaching experience.  As Forrest begins building the Bobcats’ roster, his recruiting approach will consider both basketball talent and personal character.  Forrest also emphasized that academic success and preparation for life beyond basketball will be central to the program.

As Frontier prepares to launch men’s and women’s basketball in 2027, Ellis said Forrest’s knowledge of the game and focus on building relationships will help establish a strong foundation for the men’s program.  Forrest expressed his gratitude for the opportunity and his commitment to building a program that represents Frontier well.

Forrest will begin his duties Monday.  For the latest news and updates on Bobcat Athletics, visit fccbobcats.com.

title: FAIRFIELD FALL FUN FEST
full_story:
Wren Braddock was crowned Miss Fairfield Fall Fun Fest last night in front of a large crowd.  Halen Hutson was named 1st runner up, with Peyton Harvey named 2nd runner up.  Paisley Barbre is the retiring Queen.

Tonight will feature Bingo from 5 to 7 pm.  Fire & Ice will perform from 5 to 6:30 pm, and the Fuedin Hillbillies will be on the main stage from 7 to 10 pm.

Tomorrow’s activities start at 6:30 am with the Community Breakfast at the Masonic Lodge.  The fishing derby at Leo French Park will have registration at 7:30 am and will run from 8 to 10am.  The Lemond Chrysler Center Car show registration is from 8:30 to noon with awards at 1 pm.  The baked goods competition is at 10am at the Chamber office and the Hanna House museum opens at 10am.  The WADI Headstart Kiddie Parade registration is at 10:30 at Northside School and the Parade is at 11 am.  Followed by Kiddie Corner activities and the petting zoo and the pedal pull is at Noon near the high rise.

The Cornhole tournament is at noon at City Hall. The Main Street Strength showdown is at noon in the FNB drive-thru lot.

Battle of the Bands takes the main stage at 2pm, kids activities begin at 3 pm on Saturday, and the FCHS Band will play at 5 pm followed by Tristen Brock-Jones.  Bingo is under the tent from 5 to 7 pm and Forever Abbey Road, a Beatles tribute band, will close out the Fun Fest from 7:30 to 9:30 pm.

For a complete listing of activities and times see the Fall Fun Fest Facebook page.

title: RINARD COUPLE INJURED
full_story:
One person received major injuries in a single-vehicle crash east of Mill Shoals Tuesday morning.

A westbound pickup truck driven by Cody McKinney, 34, of Rinard swerved to miss a van that was turning onto a side road, left the roadway and crashed into an embankment.  The accident happened around 8:30 am on the Burnt Prairie blacktop about a mile east of Mill Shoals.  The accident was at the crest of a hill known locally as Snowdrop Hill.

Cody McKinney was unhurt, however, his passenger, Alexis McKinney, 33, of Rinard sustained a broken leg and was airlifted to a nearby hospital for treatment of major injuries.

Fairfield Rural firemen, the White County Ambulance Service and White County deputies assisted at the scene.

title: MADAGASCAR A MUSICAL ADVENTURE
full_story:
OCC Theater is preparing to bring a wild adventure to the stage this fall with “Madagascar, A Musical Adventure!” as part of its Theatre for Young Audiences series.

Auditions are open to high school students and older and will be held at the Dr. John D. Stull Performing Arts Center on September 20th at 2 pm and September 21st at 6 pm.  Those interested in auditioning only need to attend one of the two audition sessions.

Based on the popular DreamWorks Movie, “Madagascar, A Musical Adventure!” follows some of the zoo’s most entertaining residents as they leave New York City behind.  The musical follows Alex the Lion, Marty the Zebra, Melman the Giraffe and Gloria the Hippo, along with the hilarious penguins, as they embark on an unforgettable journey from the Central Park Zoo to Madagascar.

The production is expected to bring the colorful characters, humor and adventure of the story to life for audiences of all ages.

Audition materials are available through OCC Theater at iecc.edu/occ/theater.

Following auditions and rehearsals, “Madagascar, A Musical Adventure!” is scheduled to hit the Ruth Henry Stage at the Dr. John D. Stull Performing Arts Center, at Olney Central College, November 20th through 22nd.

With familiar characters, plenty of humor and an adventure that travels from New York to the island of Madagascar, the production promises an entertaining experience for families and young theatergoers.

Those interested in auditioning are encouraged to review the audition materials and attend one of the September sessions.

title: SHEMWELL ARRESTED
full_story:
Reggie L. Shemwell, 50, of Fairfield was indicted by a Federal Grand Jury on charges he was dealing methamphetamine in Wayne and Jefferson Counties.

Shemwell, who has a lengthy criminal history in Wayne County, was charged with two meth distribution counts.  In count 1, Shemwell is accused of distributing five or more grams of methamphetamine in Wayne County.  In Count 2, he is accused of dealing 50 or more grams of meth in Jefferson County.  Both offenses allegedly occurred in May.

Shemwell remains in the custody of the US Marshals Service.  He had been scheduled for a hearing in US District Court earlier this month, but his defense attorney obtained a continuance.  A new court date has not yet been established.
